rl-sa-def.back: Slope: how steep. Aspect: which way the slope faces (the way water would run off).

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 300" font-family="sans-serif" role="img" aria-label="A compass of slope directions. North facing slopes: shade, lingering snow, thick timber.   <rect width="400" height="300" fill="#fffaf0"/>
<text x="12" y="24" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="start">Which way a slope faces</text>

  <path d="M200 158 L245 203 A64 64 0 0 1 155 203 Z" fill="#f2c70c" opacity=".7"/>
  <path d="M200 158 L155 203 A64 64 0 0 1 155 113 Z" fill="#e03131" opacity=".55"/>
  <text x="200" y="88" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">N</text><text x="200" y="240" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">S</text><text x="274" y="163" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">E</text><text x="126" y="163" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">W</text>
  <text x="200" y="52" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f6fd6" text-anchor="middle">North: shade, snow, thick timber</text>
  <text x="200" y="266" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#b85a00" text-anchor="middle">South: sun, grass, early melt</text>
  <text x="292" y="140" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="start">East:</text><text x="292" y="158" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="start">first sun</text>
  <text x="108" y="140" font-size="14" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="end">West:</text><text x="108" y="158" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="end">last sun,</text><text x="108" y="176" font-size="14" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="end">hot afternoon</text>
  <text x="200" y="292" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#2f3a2b" text-anchor="middle">Aspect = the way water would run off it</text>
</svg>

rl-sa-north30.front: How much noon sun does a 30 degree north face get in mid October?
rl-sa-north30.back: Almost none. A 30 degree south face gets about 87 percent strength.

rl-sa-stove.front: South face vs north face, in one hook?
rl-sa-stove.back: South is the stove, north is the fridge.

rl-sa-plants.front: What grows on warm south faces near Kamloops vs cool north faces?
rl-sa-plants.back: South: bunchgrass, sagebrush, open fir and pine. North: thick Douglas fir and spruce, late snow.

rl-sa-md-winter.front: BC definition of mule deer winter range slope and aspect?
rl-sa-md-winter.back: 10 to 45 percent slope, south or west aspect, below 1,500 m in shallow to moderate snow zones (85%).

rl-sa-warm.front: BC forestry warm and cool aspects?
rl-sa-warm.back: Warm about 135 to 270 degrees (SE to W). Cool about 315 to 90 degrees (NW to E).

rl-sa-cold-day.front: Cold clear morning: where to glass first?
rl-sa-cold-day.back: Sunny east and south faces (Tip). Hot noon: shady timber.

rl-sa-security.front: Why does steep broken ground matter to mule deer?
rl-sa-security.back: It is security habitat; mule deer escape up slopes into rough ground.

rl-sa-aval.back: On 30 to 45 degree slopes (Avalanche Canada). They can run far out onto flat ground below.

rl-sa-hunters.front: How did slope change hunter use in the Pennsylvania study?
rl-sa-hunters.back: Hunters were 1.25 times more likely to use an area for every 10 degree drop in slope.
